title: 6.1 Area

icans: I can partition an interval into subintervals of equal width.
I can approximate an area with left, right, and midpoint rectangles.
I can explain how lower and upper sums trap the exact area.

vocab: dividing [a, b] into n _______________, each of width Δx = (b − a)/n
the sum of rectangle areas using the minimum value of f on each ______________
the sum of rectangle areas using the maximum value of f on each ______________

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Partition: n subintervals of [a, b] each have width Δx = _______________.

blocks.stem: Partition [1, 5] into 4 subintervals of equal width. Find Δx and the subintervals.

notes: Lower and upper sums: a lower sum uses the _______________ value of f on each subinterval; an upper sum uses the maximum.

blocks.stem: f(x) = x² on [0, 2] with n = 4. Find the lower sum and the upper sum.

notes: Midpoints: the midpoint sum uses f at the _______________ of each subinterval.
Exact area: the area is the _______________ of the sums as n → ∞; for straight-sided regions, use geometry.

blocks.stem: Find the exact area under f(x) = 2x + 1 from x = 0 to x = 3.

(AP® Practice) The area under f(x) = x² + 1 from x = −1 to x = 3 is approximated with a lower sum using 4 subintervals of equal width. The approximation is
(A) 8   (B) 9   (C) 10   (D) 18
